sentences.text: They are heard.
Perused the case diary/challan papers.

2. This is the applicant's first application under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023 (Section 439 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973), as he is implicated in connection with Crime No.142/2022 registered at Police Station - Gandhwani, District Dhar (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120B of IPC.
The applicant is lodged in jail since 25.6.2025.
3. The allegation against the applicant is of committing fraud to the tune of Rs.67 Lakhs along with other co-accused persons.

It is alleged that the applicant and other co-accused persons opened a fictitious account in the name of the complainant's father Kelsingh and thereafter the amount was deposited in the said account in respect of compensation towards the land
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:6021 2 MCRC-57160-2025 acquisition, which was withdrawn without intimation to the original account holder and his family members.

4. Counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant was posted as Relationship Manager in the DCB Bank and he had opened the account, regarding which a photograph has also been filed wherein the applicant can be seen handing over the bank documents to father of the complainant Deepak Bairagi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51314810/
1 Kelsingh.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Counsel for the applicant has also submitted that this account was opened in the year 2019, whereas Kelsingh died on 21.11.2021 and till that time there was no complaint, however after his death, his son has made the complaint.
It is also submitted that the aforesaid photograph has been admitted by the son of the deceased.
Counsel for the applicant has further submitted that out of 15 witnesses, only 4 witnesses have been examined till now.
The applicant is in jail since 25.6.2025 and the final conclusion of trial is likely to take sufficient long time.

Hence, it is submitted that the bail application be allowed and applicant be released on bail.
5.
Counsel for the respondent / State, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer and it is submitted that no case for grant of bail is made out as huge amount of fraud is involved in this case.

6. Having considered the rival submissions and on perusal of the case diary and taking note of the documents filed on record as well as the photograph of the applicant handing over the bank documents to father of the complainant Kelsingh, in the considered opinion of this Court, the applicant's application deserves to be allowed.

7. Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:6021 3 MCRC-57160-2025 application filed by the applicant is allowed.

The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (rupees twenty five thousand) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.

8. However, it is directed that if the applicant is found to be involved in violation of any of the terms of this order, an application for cancellation of his bail may be filed before the trial Court itself,
which shall decide the same in accordance with law.
9.
M.Cr.C. stands allowed.
C.C. as per rules.
